reason: The sources provide over 15 verifiable claims from multiple independent sites, including details on its record-breaking longevity, its naming history with Arthur C. Clarke, and its role as the 'interplanetary internet'.
story: The oldest functional machine at another planet isn't a rover—it is a satellite named 2001 Mars Odyssey. Launched in 2001 as a tribute to Arthur C. Clarke’s science fiction masterpiece, the orbiter reached Mars by using a daring 'aerobraking' technique, skimming the atmosphere to save fuel and mission costs. Clarke himself gave his enthusiastic blessing for the name. While its primary mission was geology, Odyssey became the hero of Martian exploration by acting as the 'interplanetary internet.' It has relayed the vast majority of data from legendary rovers like Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity back to Earth. Its greatest scientific achievement was detecting massive reservoirs of water ice hidden just three feet under the Martian dust, a discovery later confirmed when the Phoenix lander physically scooped it up. Today, after more than 23 years, it continues to capture stunning horizon views that show what an astronaut would see from orbit.
angle: The longest-serving spacecraft at another world was named after a legendary sci-fi movie with the author's personal permission and has served as the 'interplanetary internet' for over 23 years.

claims.claim: 2001 Mars Odyssey is the longest-continually active spacecraft in orbit around a planet other than Earth.
The mission was launched on April 7, 2001, from Cape Canaveral.
The spacecraft arrived in Mars orbit in October 2001.
The mission was named as a tribute to Arthur C. Clarke and the film 2001: A Space Odyssey.
NASA contacted Arthur C. Clarke directly for permission, and he enthusiastically endorsed the mission name.
Odyssey used aerobraking, which uses atmospheric drag to slow down and circularize its orbit.
Using aerobraking instead of engine firing allowed the mission to use a smaller, less expensive launch vehicle.
The spacecraft’s instruments detected hydrogen, indicating water ice within one meter of the Martian surface.
In 2008, the Phoenix lander confirmed Odyssey's findings by discovering water ice on the surface.
The orbiter serves as a communications relay between Earth and various surface missions on Mars.
Odyssey relayed approximately 85% of all images and data from the Spirit and Opportunity rovers.
The spacecraft has served as a relay for the Curiosity rover during its landing and surface mission.
The MARIE radiation instrument failed in 2003 following a massive solar event.
Odyssey captured the first views of Mars showing a curving horizon and layers of atmosphere.
The original mission cost was estimated at approximately $297 million.
The spacecraft also relayed data for the Phoenix lander mission.

disputed: The exact percentage of data relayed from Spirit and Opportunity is cited as 85% in some sources [S1, S3] but over 95% in another [S5]; the script should use 'the vast majority'.
The arrival date is listed as October 24 UTC in some sources [S1] and October 23 in others [S4] due to time zone differences; the script should say 'late October'.
